subject_group: 6.2.10 Vehicle control function air data safety

versions.text: Criterion: Verify that ground provisions are safe. Standard: The air data ground safety provisions are the following: a. Allow ground checkout prior to flight for functionality. b. Have protection from the elements. c. Have protection for the crew when the heaters are on such as display notification, ground panel display notification, and circuit breaker protection. d. Allow for maintenance fault isolation to the individual probe level. e. Specific ground handling procedures to prevent any damage to the probes. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, simulation, demonstration, inspection and review of documentation. VCF air data fault isolation is verified by analysis, inspection, Hardware-In-The Loop (HITL) test to include FMET and ground test. Reference: JSSG-2008: 3.1.14, 3.1.14.1, 3.1.14.2, 3.1.14.2.4, 3.1.14.3, 3.1.14.5, 3.1.14.7, 3.2.2.4, 3.2.6.7, associated section 4 paragraphs.

Standard: The air data ground provisions: a. Allow ground checkout prior to flight for functionality. b. Protect sensors from the elements. c. Allow for maintenance fault isolation to the individual sensor-level. d. Include specific ground handling procedures to prevent damage to sensors or surrounding structure when performing maintenance or using heaters. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review documentation of ground provisions in the flight manual and checkout in the pre-flight checklist.
(2) Review maintenance procedures for protection, fault diagnostics, and handling of air data components. Demonstration.
  (1) Show that protective devices for the air data sensors can be installed and removed without causing damage to the sensors or surrounding structure and without affecting sensor calibration. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct FMET including failure detection and fault handling of the air data system when on the ground.
